subject: TriSolutions on-prem edge: BYO key delivery + gateway sealing review
messages:
From: Alice Peters <alice.peters@trisolutions.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Kickoff: TriSolutions BYOK delivery for edge gateway + sealing

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are the high-level BYOK requirements and a first-pass network diagram for the remote edge gateway we plan to deploy into our managed colos. We need to validate the key delivery and sealing design, operational rotation, and emergency eviction flow before the procurement window closes. Top items we need aligned on: 

- Hardware HSM type: our procurement is leaning to SafeKey 7300 (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) — we need to confirm compatibility with Redwood's keystore-proxy model.
- Delivery method: secure courier (encrypted USB sealed) vs. in-person handoff to on-site custodian with split-witness.
- Initial sealing: remote attestation + KMS wrapped import; should the host run a TPM-based root-of-trust to validate the image prior to unseal?
- Rotation cadence and operator model: 30/90/365 day splits? Who carries rotation entitlement in the operator split?
- Audit/evidence: proof-of-destruction for replaced keys, and KMS audit logs ingestion into our SIEM (we'll provide endpoints).

Can we schedule a short review this week? I've copied Marissa and Laura for ops and security alignment. I've included a Drive folder with the diagram and procurement draft.

Attachments: tri_byo_requirements.pdf, edge-network-diagram-v2.png, ops-procurement-sla-draft.docx

Thanks,
Alice Peters
Head of Infrastructure Security
TriSolutions

--

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alice Peters <alice.peters@trisolutions.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: TriSolutions BYOK delivery for edge gateway + sealing

Alice —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. High level response before we meet:

1) HSM compatibility: SafeKey 7300 looks fine from an API perspective. Our keystore-proxy supports PKCS#11 import and wrapped-key ingestion (AES wrap + asymmetric unwrap in HSM). We'll validate firmware compatibility in a lab before any handoff.

2) Delivery: Split-witness courier + operator handoff is our recommended default for remote colo. That avoids single-person custody. If you prefer a physical sealed USB, we require immediate entropy-checksum verification on receipt and a rendezvous attestation prior to import.

3) Sealing & attestation: Yes — TPM-based measured boot on the gateway is the right call. Redwood's private deployment package can require firmware measurements (PCRs) and a remote attestation challenge before issuing unseal tokens to the KMS proxy. We'll provide the attestation challenge script as part of the on-prem agent.

4) Rotation model: propose two-tier: short-lived session KEKs (30d) rotated by on-site operator automation and long-lived wrapping keys (annual 365d) stored in customer HSM with split-custody. Operator entitlements are scoped: Redwood ops gets the orchestration hooks but cannot export unwrapped material.

5) Audit/evidence: we can stream KMS audit events (JSON lines) to your SIEM over an MTLS TLS endpoint. Proof-of-destruction: we can produce signed metadata from the HSM when a key is zeroized (attested timestamp + operator signature).

Next step: 30-minute call to review the attached diagram and to align on a sample handoff checklist. Are you available 11/15 at 10:00am PT?

- Rishi
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

--

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alice Peters <alice.peters@trisolutions.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: TriSolutions BYOK delivery for edge gateway + sealing

On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 09:03 AM Rishi wrote:
> Next step: 30-minute call to review the attached diagram and to align on a sample handoff checklist. Are you available 11/15 at 10:00am PT?

We pulled the network diagram into our lab review. A couple of ops-specific notes we should discuss on the call: 

- Network placement: the edge gateway should sit behind an egress-filtering firewall with outbound whitelists limited to Redwood broker endpoints and your SIEM ingestion endpoints. No direct internet egress except for telemetry to approved destinations.
- Management plane: require an out-of-band management NIC and a jumpbox inside your colo project. Management traffic for key import must be physically isolated (VLAN or separate interface) from tenant data lanes.
- Time sync: HSMs and attestation rely on tight NTP. We'll include an NTP bastion that peers only to your internal NTP pool and Redwood's monitoring for drift alerts.
- Emergency fallback: recommend an emergency-wrapper (pre-provisioned wrapped-key) held by an escrow service (split between TriSolutions and an independent custodian) so we can recover service without exposing raw key material.

I'll bring a short handoff checklist (hardware receipt, serial validation, firmware checksum, witness log) to the call.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Peters <alice.peters@trisolutions.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: TriSolutions BYOK delivery for edge gateway + sealing

Thanks all — good call earlier today. Summary and immediate action items (ops checklist attached):

Summary of agreed points:
- SafeKey 7300 is supported for wrapped-key import via PKCS#11.
- Delivery model: split-witness handoff by default; sealed USB allowed only with rendezvous attestation.
- Attestation: TPM measured boot required; Redwood agent will run challenge and only issue unseal tokens post-verified PCR set.
- Network: management plane on separate NIC + VLAN, strict outbound whitelist to Redwood broker and your SIEM.
- Rotation: KEKs rotated every 30 days via agent-managed automation; wrapping master keys rotated annually and can only be rotated by customer-initiated HSM ceremony.
- Evidence: HSM-signed zeroize receipts and continuous KMS audit stream to TriSolutions SIEM.

Immediate action items:
1) TriSolutions to confirm courier vs. on-site custodian selection by 2026-11-18. (Alice)
2) Rishi to provide attestation script and PCR policy document by 11/19. (Rishi)
3) Karthik to publish network ACL template and NTP bastion config by 11/20. (Karthik)
4) Marissa to finalize the handoff checklist (attached) and ops runbook for the first 3 months. (Marissa)

Attachments: tri_byo_requirements.pdf, edge-network-diagram-v2.png, ops-procurement-sla-draft.docx, tri_edge_handoff_checklist_v1.md

Notes on edge-case behavior:
- If the HSM firmware fails attestation, the agent will put the device into an "isolated recv" state and refuse import; operator escalation required with vendor-signed firmware image to proceed.
- For disaster scenarios where the on-site operator is unreachable, Redwood can support a pre-agreed emergency unwrap via split-escrow (requires three-party signatures and a documented chain-of-approval).

I'll circulate the updated runbook after I fold in your comments.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Private Deployments Ops
Redwood Inference
